draft.title: The Holocaust
card: The Holocaust was the planned, state-run murder of about six million Jews by Nazi Germany and its collaborators. It is an example of genocide, the attempt to destroy a whole people.
The Nazis also murdered Roma, disabled people and others, including Soviet prisoners of war. Many others were persecuted for their politics, beliefs or identity.
Persecution grew in stages. Jews were first defined and excluded by laws, such as the Nuremberg Laws of 1935. Violence followed, then forced removal into ghettos.

During the war, killing became organised on a huge scale. Mass shootings in occupied territory came first. Later, the Nazis built camps in occupied Poland, such as Auschwitz-Birkenau, that were designed to kill.
draft.remember: The Holocaust was a planned genocide that moved from legal exclusion to mass murder.

a.q: Why do historians describe the Holocaust as a genocide?
opts: It was a planned effort to destroy a whole people
It happened mainly during the fighting of a war
It was carried out by soldiers acting without orders
It targeted only people who opposed the Nazi Party
a.why: The Nazi state planned and organised the murder of Jews as a people. The killing was not random wartime violence, and it was not limited to political opponents, since victims were targeted for who they were.
a.clue: Think about the word planned and who was targeted.

b.q: A student says the Holocaust began with the opening of the killing camps in Poland. Which reply is best supported by the card?
opts: It built up in stages, starting with laws that excluded Jews
It began in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland
It began suddenly once the war turned against Germany
It began with attacks on Roma, not Jews
b.why: Persecution began with laws such as the Nuremberg Laws of 1935, long before the camps designed to kill. The camps were a later stage of a process that had been growing for years, so the student's view leaves out the earlier steps.
b.clue: Look at what came before the camps.

a.best: It was a planned effort to destroy a whole people

b.best: It built up in stages, starting with laws that excluded Jews
